title: Argentina Predicted to Win: v2-noise-off-mid Condition
summary: In the v2-noise-off-mid condition, Argentina was predicted to win with 80% confidence, despite the injection of off-topic sports news.

sections.title: Narrative Result
sections.content:
## Narrative Result

In the `v2-noise-off-mid` condition, Argentina was predicted to win the Copa America 2024 final with 80% confidence. The model’s prediction was based on the narrative that “Argentina is analyzed as the favorite with experience and depth,” and that they “confides in its history of victories and solid defense.”  Despite the injection of an off-topic sports news document (“noise-off”), the prediction remained consistent. 

The injected document, described as containing “plausible sports-news noise, intentionally not useful for predicting Argentina vs Colombia,” was flagged as having “low” noise contamination. Keyword counts support this assessment; while `football_noise` mentions increased from 0 to 4 following injection, mentions of Argentina (6) and Colombia (4) remained relatively stable.  Notably, James Rodriguez received 6 mentions.

The `difference_vs_baseline` assessment confirms that the core narrative was unaffected: “The injected document contained off-topic sports news…but the core narrative remains focused on Argentina as the favorite.” The model did not `used_injected_document` in its reasoning.  The simulation completed successfully (`status: completed`) with 5 posts, 0 comments, and 13 traces. The artifact directory is `runs/s2_issue19_deepinfra/gemma/v2-noise-off-mid-12`.  The top discussed posts, such as “Argentina is analyzed as the favorite with experience and depth,” reinforce the prediction.

sections.title: Injection Effect
sections.content:
## Injection Effect

In the `v2-noise-off-mid` condition, the injection of an off-topic sports news document had minimal impact on the prediction. Despite the injection of the `noise-off` document, Argentina was still predicted to win with 80% confidence. The `noise_contamination` was assessed as “low,” and the model did not `used_injected_document` in its reasoning. 

The injected document, as described in `Post 5 by opta_preview_summary_427`, contained “plausible sports-news noise, intentionally not useful for predicting Argentina vs Colombia.” This is reflected in the keyword counts, where `football_noise` increased to 4 mentions after injection, but the mentions of the teams remained relatively stable (Argentina: 6, Colombia: 4). The `difference_vs_baseline` assessment specifically states that “the core narrative remains focused on Argentina as the favorite.” The simulation completed successfully, with one scheduled event fired in round 6 (`fired_round: 6`, `fired_round_index: 5`). The top discussed posts, such as “Argentina is analyzed as the favorite with experience and depth” (`Post 1 by opta_preview_summary_427`), continued to support Argentina as the favored team.
